examples.question_text: A loan of $\$18\,000$ charges $8.4\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly. Repayments of $\$900$ are made at the end of each quarter. Write the recurrence relation for the balance $A_n$ after $n$ repayments, including the initial value.
examples.solution_text:
The quarterly interest rate is $r=\dfrac{0.084}{4}=0.021$.
Interest is added before each repayment is subtracted.
$\begin{align*}A_0&=18\,000\\A_n&=A_{n-1}(1.021)-900\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A loan of $\$20\,000$ charges $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Repayments of $\$700$ are made at the end of each month. Expand the balances after the first three repayments. Hence write an expanded series expression for $A_n$ and for the balance after $2$ years, while the debt remains outstanding.
examples.solution_text:
The monthly interest rate is $r=\dfrac{0.072}{12}=0.006$, so $A_0=20\,000$ and $A_n=A_{n-1}(1.006)-700$.
After the first repayment:
$A_1=20\,000(1.006)-700$.
After the second repayment:
$\begin{align*}A_2&=[20\,000(1.006)-700](1.006)-700\\&=20\,000(1.006)^2-700(1.006)-700\end{align*}$
After the third repayment:
$\begin{align*}A_3&=[20\,000(1.006)^2-700(1.006)-700](1.006)-700\\&=20\,000(1.006)^3-700(1.006)^2-700(1.006)-700\end{align*}$
The principal grows for $n$ months. The first repayment has $n-1$ remaining growth periods; the final repayment has none.
$A_n=20\,000(1.006)^n-700(1.006)^{n-1}-700(1.006)^{n-2}-\cdots-700$.
The subtracted terms form a geometric series with first term $700$, common ratio $1.006$ and $n$ terms when written in ascending powers.
For $2$ years, $n=2\times12=24$:
$A_{24}=20\,000(1.006)^{24}-700(1.006)^{23}-700(1.006)^{22}-\cdots-700$.

examples.question_text: A reducing balance loan of $\$10\,000$ charges $12\%$ p.a. compounded monthly, with repayments of $\$400$ at the end of each month. Calculate the interest charged over the first $4$ months. Compare it with a flat-rate loan of $\$10\,000$ at $9\%$ p.a. over the same period. Keep full precision until rounding the totals and difference to the nearest cent.
examples.solution_text:
The monthly rate is $r=\dfrac{0.12}{12}=0.01$. Each month's interest is $0.01$ times its starting balance.
$\begin{align*}I_1&=10\,000(0.01)=100\\A_1&=10\,000+100-400=9700\\I_2&=9700(0.01)=97\\A_2&=9700+97-400=9397\\I_3&=9397(0.01)=93.97\\A_3&=9397+93.97-400=9090.97\\I_4&=9090.97(0.01)=90.9097\end{align*}$
Reducing balance interest:
$\begin{align*}I_{\mathrm{reducing}}&=100+97+93.97+90.9097\\&=381.8797\\&\approx\$381.88\end{align*}$
Flat-rate interest is calculated on the original principal:
$\begin{align*}I_{\mathrm{flat}}&=10\,000(0.09)\dfrac{4}{12}\\&=\$300.00\end{align*}$
The difference is $381.8797-300\approx\$81.88$. The reducing balance loan charges $\$81.88$ more interest over these four months.

examples.question_text: A loan of $\$60\,000$ charges $9.6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Repayments of $\$450$ are made at the end of each month. Explain why the balance increases despite the repayments.
examples.solution_text:
The monthly rate is $r=\dfrac{0.096}{12}=0.008$.
First month's interest:
$\begin{align*}I_1&=60\,000(0.008)\\&=\$480\end{align*}$
Balance after the first repayment:
$\begin{align*}A_1&=60\,000(1.008)-450\\&=\$60\,030\end{align*}$
The repayment is $\$30$ less than the interest charged. The balance increases, so the next month's interest is larger. With the same rate and repayment, the balance continues to increase.

examples.derivation: Independently obtained the quarterly rate 0.084/4=0.021. Adding quarterly interest before subtracting the end-of-quarter repayment gives A_n=1.021A_{n-1}-900, with A_0=18000. This follows the recurrence example at source lines 247–269.

Independently obtained the monthly growth factor 1.006. Successive substitution gives A_1=20000(1.006)-700; A_2=20000(1.006)^2-700(1.006)-700; and A_3=20000(1.006)^3-700(1.006)^2-700(1.006)-700. After n repayments, the principal has exponent n and the n repayment terms have exponents n-1 through 0. Two years gives 24 repayments and the stated A_24 expression. The balance remains positive after 24 repayments. Reversing the repayment terms into ascending powers gives first term 700 and common ratio 1.006. The derivation follows source lines 2056–2074 and 3166–3199 without carrying over the source's erroneous 1.08 factor.

Independently calculated monthly interest of 100, 97, 93.97 and 90.9097 from starting balances 10000, 9700, 9397 and 9090.97. Their sum is 381.8797, rounding to $381.88. Flat-rate interest is 10000×0.09×4/12=$300.00. The unrounded difference is 81.8797, rounding to $81.88 more for the reducing balance loan. This uses the successive-balance and flat-rate comparison method at source lines 1914–1953.

Independently obtained the monthly rate 0.096/12=0.008, first interest charge 60000×0.008=$480, and first closing balance 60000×1.008-450=$60030. The repayment falls $30 short of the interest. Subsequent interest increases with the outstanding balance, so the unchanged repayment continues to be insufficient. This follows source lines 315–329 and 2176–2186.
